recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-6022; future performer/author/verifier/function/asserter distinctions should be handled through their dedicated later issues rather than this short-description clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-6022 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request from DSTU1 asking to change Observation.performer short from 'Who did the observation' to 'Who is responsible for the observation'; the possible Author alias was deferred as a separate change.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit 8576998aaf8b269268d36749fc43b0dd3a180581, which changed source/observation/observation-spreadsheet.xml to the requested wording. Later source rework, including 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157, carried the same short into source/observation/structuredefinition-Observation.xml.
additional_context: Observation is active in source/fhir.ini. Later related issues FHIR-13838, FHIR-41405, and FHIR-46683 deal with performer role/function extension semantics, adding Group as an allowed performer target, and a rejected asserter element request; none supersede the FHIR-6022 short description. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-6022 found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/observation/structuredefinition-Observation.xml currently has <short value="Who is responsible for the observation"/> for Observation.performer, and current-source searches did not find the old 'Who did the observation' short in Observation source.

related_jiras.note: Later performer role/function extension issue and linked Zulip discussion confirm author/verifier distinctions were handled separately from the base short description.
Later added Group as an allowed Observation.performer target while preserving the FHIR-6022 short description.
Later no-change request for an Observation.asserter element did not replace the performer model or short description.
